resources.string: A file manager for doing real work on your phone, without reaching for a PC. Open source, no ads, no accounts, no telemetry.
Most of Filet works the way you would expect. These three do not, and they are the reason it exists.
Only all-files access really matters, and even that can be refused — you will just be limited to folders you pick by hand.

Long-press to select, tap to add more. Copy or Move puts files on the clipboard; open another folder and paste from the top bar.
This is early, and it is a one-person project. Expect rough edges.
You can skip any of these. Filet still opens without them.
Progress for long jobs — copying, indexing, signing. Optional.
The ordinary storage permission, on Android versions that still have one.
Browse, move and edit anything on this device. Android asks for this on its own Settings screen, so you will be sent there and back. Without it, only folders you pick by hand are visible.
Lets apps signed with the same key read and write file provenance and the shared job ledger.
A folder from your storage, on the home screen.
